description: Nine-day Brahmotsavam at America's first traditional Hindu temple, the Sri Venkateswara Temple in Pittsburgh.
long_description: The Sri Venkateswara Temple in Penn Hills — the first traditional Hindu temple built in America (1977) — celebrates its annual Brahmotsavam with nine days of elaborate Vedic rituals, processions, and cultural programs. Modeled after the famous Tirumala temple in India, this is one of the most sacred Hindu celebrations in North America. Thousands of devotees travel from across the country for this festival.
venue_info: 1230 S McCully Dr, Penn Hills, PA 15235. Ample parking. Multi-day event — check temple website for daily schedule. Prasadam served. Accommodation suggestions on temple website.

***GRAB A DRINK AND YOU ARE ALL SET TO FLEX YOUR LANGUAGE CAPACITY. YOU NEED TO GET AT LEAST A DRINK OR FOOD :) To get the event going and show support. We know that you like our events. P.S. : We have non-alcoholic drinks as well.***

We have a tiny venue and we hit capacity often and early arrival is suggested.

We have the discretion to decide entry.

All languages are welcome! However we don't guarantee the availability of a partner in that particular language, you would like to exchange.
HOW IT WORKS : We will try to assign tables for each represented languages and will direct attendees to their respective tables accordingly. All languages are welcome! However we don't guarantee the availability of a partner in that particular language, you would like to exchange.

Rules to abide :

1. Event is free and 21+ (bring ID).
2. Be respectful to your counterparts and give them a chance to exchange with others as well.
3. We all are native speakers of one or two languages and be willing to help others and try to accommodate as much as possible.
4. If you don't speak the other person's required language, LEAVE THEM ALONE.
5. Rude or aggressive members are removed from the group at an organizers discretion.
6. This is a face-to-face language exchange event. DO NOT try to arrange an online meeting, by using the comment box or direct message.
7. Most of our members complained about people writing in the comment box. Since it sends notification to all attendees. If you have any questions, send a message to the organizers. Don't write in the comment box.
8. We have ZERO TOLERANCE for solicitation. We don't allow anyone to run their own agenda at the Event. If you are interested to promote/sponsor/collaborate; contact us via ([info@merevents.com](mailto:info@merevents.com)).

long_description:
**WHAT TO EXPECT**
Kirtan Soulfest is simply a transcendental party guaranteed to uplift you mentally, physically, and emotionally. The sacred mantras chanted in a call-and-response manner is the prescribed method given in the Vedas to link the inner divinity within all of us. This link connects us to the real happiness, peace and love we are all searching for.
Come with an open heart, dance and leave with an overflow of LOVE!

**WHAT IS MANTRA MEDITATION?**
Mantra Meditation is a type of Sound Bath and Yoga which is an immersive experience combining powerful soundwaves and group singing/chanting to help individuals better connect with their inner selves. Yoga means to unite, Mantra Meditation will help unite your mind to your body and soul.
The sounds and singing during a Mantra Meditation session are an invitation to journey into a deeper state of consciousness as an opportunity to gain perspective on what's going on within you. The goal of the experience is to invite deep relaxation, restoration and explore self-inquiry and self-discovery.

**WHO IS THIS FOR?**
Mantra Meditation is a growing movement in North America derived from ancient Vedic traditions and is applicable to everyone. However, some examples of individuals who might greatly benefit from Mantra Meditation are:

* If you want to relax, refresh and nourish yourself
* Stress, anxiety, or overwhelm dominate your life
* You're challenged by illness
* Grieving the loss of someone or even the past
* You're seeking a breakthrough in understanding your higher purpose
* You're looking to deepen your healing wisdom and spiritual connection
* You're wanting to connect with a community of compassionate, inclusive and supportive beings alike

Mantra meditation has different effects on everyone and is a deeply personal interaction with the sound vibrations.

**THE BOOK**
Heart Lamp: Selected Stories
In the twelve stories of Heart Lamp, Banu Mushtaq exquisitely captures the everyday lives of women and girls in Muslim communities in southern India. Published originally in the Kannada language between 1990 and 2023, praised for their dry and gentle humour, these portraits of family and community tensions testify to Mushtaq’s years as a journalist and lawyer, in which she tirelessly championed women’s rights and protested all forms of caste and religiou
long_description:
**THE BOOK**
Heart Lamp: Selected Stories
In the twelve stories of Heart Lamp, Banu Mushtaq exquisitely captures the everyday lives of women and girls in Muslim communities in southern India. Published originally in the Kannada language between 1990 and 2023, praised for their dry and gentle humour, these portraits of family and community tensions testify to Mushtaq’s years as a journalist and lawyer, in which she tirelessly championed women’s rights and protested all forms of caste and religious oppression. Written in a style at once witty, vivid, colloquial, moving and excoriating, it’s in her characters – the sparky children, the audacious grandmothers, the buffoonish maulvis and thug brothers, the oft-hapless husbands, and the mothers above all, surviving their feelings at great cost – that Mushtaq emerges as an astonishing writer and observer of human nature, building disconcerting emotional heights out of a rich spoken style. Her opus has garnered both censure from conservative quarters as well India’s most prestigious literary awards; this is a collection sure to be read for years to come.

**THE AUTHOR**
Banu Mushtaq (ಬಾನು ಮುಷ್ತಾಕ್, born 1948) is an activist, lawyer and writer from the southern Indian state of Karnataka. She writes in the Kannada language and her works have also been published in Urdu, Hindi, Tamil, Malayalam and, most recently, English.

What is Kirtan:
Kirtan is the Yoga of Devotion (Bhakti Yoga). Derived from a Sanskrit root meaning to call, recite, praise, or glorify, put simply, kirtan is the act of praising and glorifying the Divine.

Why Kirtan:
Chanting Kirtan is a devotional practice that helps to uplift the mind, open the heart and bring inner peace. It is the fastest, easiest and most joyful way to achieve peace of mind. The mantras are mystical universal sounds that resonate with our chakras and remove negative energies. So, it is important that we chant so that we can benefit from this powerful healing energy.

long_description:
Curious how to start learning something? Want to chat with someone of another discipline? Need a place to work on a project and share it with others? ISG is a social, game development focused work group that encourages people of all skill levels and disciplines to come together and collaborate for the benefit of all.

This is a great place to begin your game development journey and learn from fellow game creators as they work on their projects.

**Bring your laptop** and any software you will need to work on your game/art/music.

How it Works:

• Show up, introduce yourself, let everyone know what you hope to accomplish

• Ask for help with anything, get to know others, share your projects, or enjoy the company of others as you work!

• Share your highs and lows, high fives all around

***

How to find us:
It can be kind of hard to find us! We are on the 4th floor of the Armory building. Follow the signs to the restrooms, and nearby you'll find the stairs and the elevator. Take one of those to the fourth floor and look for the Seattle Indies banner.

***

Accessibility information:
There is paid street parking all around the neighborhood. There are paid parking garages at 516 Harrison St, 650 3rd Ave N, and at the corner of 5th Ave N and Harrison St. The Seattle Center has nearby bus stops serviced by the 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 13, 15, 17, 18, 19, 24, 32, 33, D Line, and the monorail. The venue is listed as wheelchair accessible. The Seattle Center has additional accessibility information available on their website here: http://www.seattlecenter.com/about/accessibility.aspx

If you are coming by Light Rail it is best to get off at Westlake Station and then ride the Monorail over to the Seattle Center which drops you off right at the Armory.

***

Seattle Indies strives to be an inclusive and welcoming community for everyone. By attending our events, you are agreeing to follow our code of conduct (https://www.seattleindies.org/code-of-conduct/).

long_description:
# 🎉 Boston Festival of Chariots (Ratha Yatra) – A Celebration of Joy, Culture & Spirituality!

Experience one of India's most beloved and vibrant cultural festivals—right here in Boston!
For centuries, the sacred Festival of Chariots (Ratha Yatra) has been celebrated in the holy city of Jagannath Puri, India, where hundreds of thousands gather to welcome Lord Jagannath, "The Lord of the Universe," along with His brother Baladeva and sister Subhadra. Amidst joyful chanting, colorful processions, music, and dancing, devotees pull magnificent chariots through the streets in a grand expression of love and devotion.
Now, this timeless festival comes to Boston!
Join us for a day filled with happiness, community, culture, and spiritual inspiration as we bring the ancient tradition of Ratha Yatra to the heart of the city.
✨ **Festival Highlights**
• Pull the beautifully decorated chariot of Lord Jagannath
• Experience joyful kirtan (live mantra music) and dancing
• Learn simple and powerful mantra meditation practices
• Meet friendly monks and spiritual practitioners at interactive Q&A booths
• Explore fascinating exhibits and cultural displays
• Browse spiritual books, gifts, and cultural artifacts
• Enjoy henna art and family-friendly activities for children
• Make meaningful connections and new friendships
• Savor a delicious **FREE vegetarian feast**
Lord Jagannath is celebrated not only as the Lord of the Universe but as the embodiment of divine love, compassion, and joy. This festival is an opportunity to step away from the pressures of daily life and immerse yourself in an atmosphere of celebration, positivity, and spiritual upliftment.
Whether you're seeking cultural enrichment, inner peace, family fun, or simply a unique experience, the Boston Festival of Chariots has something for everyone.
🌸 Come celebrate. Sing. Dance. Connect. Feast.
🌸 Discover a tradition that has inspired millions around the world.
🌸 Leave feeling refreshed, uplifted, and inspired.

We appreciate advance registration.

### **Chanting mantras and prayers are elements of the Bhakti Yoga path which leads to union with the Divine Consciousness. Chanting calms the nerves, purifies the emotions, heals the body and opens the heart. It elevates and concentrates the mind, preparing one for silent mantra repetition, meditation and communion with the Divine. Chanting done with a devotional attitude lifts the emotions toward selfless, divine love.**

***

**Acharya Mangalananda** has learned by deep immersion the traditional spiritual music of India. His kirtan is couched in the mystical ragas of India and is full of the lively ecstatic joy of the Divine Names. Mangalananda has toured extensively throughout India, Europe and the USA, presenting kirtan concerts, yoga classes and workshop retreats. He is an Acharya (an appointed Spiritual Teacher) of Ma Anandamayi Ashram in Omkareshwar / Indore in the lineage of Sri Anandamayi Ma.

organizer: Hindi Poetry Open Mic — Bay Area
long_description:
This will be our 5th meeting of the Bay area Hindi Urdu poetry open Mic Mehfil.

Chaliye, shuru karte hain.
This is it, another evening for poetic minds to connect and celebrate poetery - Hindi Poetry Open Mic in the South Bay. We’re gathering at the Warm springs park Freemont for an evening of Hindi kavita under the trees.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/AFhfr3RKVzrNs6Nz8

Here’s how it works:
Show up by 5:30 PM. We’ll settle in, do quick intros, and kick off the open mic. Sign up on the spot if you’d like to share — you get 3-5 minutes to read original work, recite a classic, or share anything that moves you. Prefer to just listen? That’s equally welcome. Every mehfil needs its audience.

What to bring:
Yourself. Maybe a poem. Maybe just your ears. If you want to go the extra mile, bring a blanket to sit on and some chai in a thermos — we’re keeping this simple.

Who is this for?
Anyone who loves poetry — whether you write it, read it, or just feel it. If you grew up hearing kavita at home, if you scribble shayari in your Notes app, if you’ve been looking for your people — this is the space.

Logistics:
We’ll in the park, look for the group with the obvious poetry energy or call Shekhar at 9193389676. Free parking is available on surrounding streets. The park closes at 9 PM but we’ll wrap up by 7:30.

long_description:
In tango, the giro is more than a turn - it’s a language of rotation, power, and elegant control. This 8-week Intermediate course is designed to deepen your understanding of giros in both parallel and cross-system, while integrating advanced elements like sacadas, patadas, and varied embrace styles.
**Main Focus:**

* *Isolation and connection* \- separate the upper and lower body for precise control
* *Continuity of torsion and rotation* \- lead and follow dynamics that flow
* *Left and right giro from the back cross* \- in both parallel and cross\-system
* *Turning technique* \- understand system principles and execute effortlessly

**Additional Explorations:**

* Octagonal, square, and triangular giro structures
* Modern vs. milonguero-style turns – combine the best of both worlds
* Giro with sacada on the open step
* Giro with patada - style meets momentum
* The leader’s axis and its impact on the turn

long_description:
Flow Beneath the Bells: Traditional Yoga at the Netherlands Carillon

Cost: Free
Level: Beginner Friendly

Take a break from the noise and join us for a refreshing hour of yoga in one of Arlington’s most beautiful outdoor spaces.

Whether you’ve been practicing for years or can’t touch your toes without negotiating first, you’re welcome here. This class is designed for beginners, but experienced practitioners will also enjoy the flow.

During this session we’ll:

• Learn foundational yoga poses
• Explore simple breathing techniques to reduce stress and improve focus
• Build strength, balance, and flexibility
• Stretch out tight muscles from work, running, cycling, or life in general
• Spend an hour moving, breathing, and reconnecting with ourselves

No pressure. No competition. No yoga experience required.

What to Bring

• A yoga mat or large towel
• Water
• Comfortable clothes you can move in
• An open mind

A Few Quick Notes

• Please arrive a few minutes early so we can start on time.
• Avoid a heavy meal right before class. Light snacks are fine.
• If your plans change, please update your RSVP so someone else can join.

Safety Disclaimer

Please consult your healthcare provider before starting any exercise program, including yoga. Participate at your own pace and listen to your body. Modify or skip any movement that doesn’t feel right for you. By attending this class, you acknowledge that you are responsible for your own health and well-being and participate voluntarily.

long_description:
**Mysore Style Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga**
Mysore Style Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga is named after the city in South India; Mysore where this transformative practice originated from the co-founders Krishnamacharya & K. Pattabhi Jois nearly 90 years ago. Mysore style means you work at your own pace while the teacher provides tailored instruction from giving postures, asking questions, & giving hands-on adjustments when necessary. The beauty of Mysore is you don’t need to keep up with the teacher or other students in the room since it is an individual practice similar to an individual playing a song on a guitar, doing a dance or doing a kata in martial arts in a customized way. Since the same postures are repeated each time you can memorize the sequence giving you practice to take home with you or wherever you roam on Mother Earth.
Bio:
Shane has had daily Mysore yoga practice for nearly 20 years. He practiced and studied with/ Master teachers in North America & India including Richard Freeman, Mary Taylor, Rolf Naujokat, & Marci Naujokat. Shane has had a daily yoga practice since 2003 & has been teaching yoga since 2004.

long_description:
**MLK Library - Room 302E**

So many of us have a bucket list of things we hope to do or achieve before we “kick the bucket”! But do we also need to consider creating a spiritual bucket list – not just a list of things we want to do, but of things we want to be? And do we wait to one day just become these things, or are these things we can – and should we – be working on right now, day by day?

What makes a bucket list meaningful is that it be a reflection of what you value and desire – a tool to help push ourselves to grow and develop and fulfill our highest aspirations. Things like skydiving, traveling, running a marathon, and buying a house are common to-do’s helping us achieve our material aspirations. But what about considering our ultimate to-do’s to fulfill our spiritual purpose? What if we aspired to grow spiritually, to be kinder and more virtuous people, to help others in need? Do we need to wait for some future time to do these things, or can we actually draw closer every day to achieving these goals through our daily choices and spiritual habits? What would it look like to live a life designed around reaching these spiritual goals and reaching our true, spiritual purpose? How can we support each other in checking off our spiritual bucket lists?

Come join a different kind of conversation – one that welcomes every perspective in a search for the deeper truths that unite us – as we discuss the spiritual perspective offered by the Bahá’í Teachings on fulfilling our spiritual purpose. Please join us for a lively discussion as we explore how we can each live a life of spiritual growth and fulfillment and create communities that support each and every one of us.

*“Material progress insures the happiness of the human world. Spiritual progress insures the happiness and eternal continuance of the soul.”* – Bahá’í Teachings

**\*\*\* This event is free and open to all regardless of background or belief. Donations will not be accepted.**

long_description:
**Jyeshtabhishekam – Annual Sacred Ceremony**

The Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago (HTGC) invites devotees to the annual Jyeshtabhishekam ceremony, a deeply significant ritual observance in the Hindu calendar.

The ceremony includes:
- **Rudra Homam** – Sacred fire ritual invoking Lord Shiva
- **Chandi Homam** – Fire ritual honoring Goddess Chandi/Durga
- Abhishekam (sacred bathing) of the deities
- Vedic chanting by temple priests

This is one of the most important annual rituals at HTGC and draws devotees from across the greater Chicago area.

**Details:**
- Date: Sunday, June 28, 2026
- Location: Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago, 10915 Lemont Rd, Lemont, IL
- Admission: Free and open to all devotees

organizer: Real Talk Christianity: Navigating Doubt in Hard Seasons
long_description:
**About This Group**

Real Talk Christianity is an interactive, discussion-based gathering—not a lecture or formal church service. We make room for questions, struggles, and doubt that come from a genuine desire to seek God.

**Meeting Details**

Monday, 7–9 PM | South Bay Coffee Shop Location will be sent to you once you RSVP.

**What to Expect**

This is the first gathering of Real Talk Christianity, an emotionally honest Christian community for people struggling to reconcile deep faith with difficult lived experience.

We’re starting with Elijah—a Bible character who embodies both spiritual power and deep exhaustion. James 5:17 says, “Elijah was a man just like us.” He stood on Mount Carmel in fire and faith, then ran into the wilderness wanting to die (1 Kings 19). God didn’t scold him; He met him with rest, food, companionship, and a gentle voice.

**This night is for anyone who:**

* Feels spiritually weary, tested, or distant from God
* Is questioning, doubting, or confused but still seeking
* Wants honest, Christ-centered conversation without shame or performance
* Is curious about Christianity or newly exploring faith

**The Evening Flow**

7:00–7:20 PM — Settle In Optional snacks / shared meal, casual connection

7:20–7:30 PM — Opening Prayer Centering our time on God’s presence and guidance

7:30–7:40 PM — Optional Check-In Simple prompt: “What’s something you’re carrying into tonight?”  7:40–7:50 PM — Praise & Worship One contemporary song to shift the atmosphere and welcome the Holy Spirit

7:50–8:40 PM — Scripture & Real Talk: Elijah
  We’ll read 1 Kings 19:1–18 and James 5:17, then explore:
* Where do you see yourself in Elijah’s story (the high, the low, or both)?
* What do you need from God right now that Elijah received (rest, food, companionship, a gentle word)?

Participation is always voluntary. Some share deeply; others listen and reflect.

8:40–8:55 PM — Optional Prayer Requests & Closing Prayer  Leaving encouraged, not “fixed.”

Steve Franconeri, PhD, Northwestern University Professor of cognitive psychology, developed *[Point Taken](https://pointtaken.social/)*, a game easy to master at any age, that is designed to turn heated arguments into a joint exploration supported by mutual respect and honest thinking. He will explain his reasoning and the research behind it the game, then we will play it and provide feedback.

It's a great follow up to ISC's program last fall -- *Your Brain on Misinformation --* when Dr. Matthew Facciani presented his work for *Misguided: Where Misinformation Starts, How It Spreads, and What to Do About It.* Attendees were very interested in how to persuade relatives discussing politics and had a lively post-presentation conversation about how to have productive non-argumentative conversations. This game will be a great exercise in that effort but you certainly don't need to have gone to that event to attend this one.

**Monday, June 29, 2026**
**6:00pm - 9:00pm-ish (game presentation at 6:30)**
**[Half Sour](https://halfsourchicago.com/)**, 755 S Clark St., Chicago, IL ([map](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Half+Sour/@41.8725394,-87.6305898,18.24z/data=!4m6!3m5!1s0x880e2c970f9401cf:0xcadfde30a7663d8d!8m2!3d41.872448!4d-87.630322!16s%2Fg%2F11hbkts6fs?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDYwMy4xIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D)) at Polk St.
**[Registration on EventBrite](https://ScienceSocial12.eventbrite.com)** is strongly recommended and very much appreciated. Tix $0-10 donation.
You're responsible for your own refreshments.

***See you there!!***

long_description:
**Welcome to Bhakti Night** \- an evening dedicated to the wisdom and practice of *bhakti-yoga*.

The evening begins with a soul-stirring *kirtan*, a musical form of meditation, where the air will resonate with melodious chants and the rhythmic beats of traditional instruments. As the sweet sound vibrations fill the room, you'll find your heart opening up, and any stress or worries gently dissipate, replaced by a profound sense of peace and contentment. The *kirtan* is followed by a talk on teachings from the ancient yoga tradition which is always thought provoking and even entertaining!

As the night draws to a close, we'll conclude with a delightful vegetarian dinner. Savor the sanctified dishes, lovingly prepared with devotion, and experience how food can be an offering of love and nourishment for the soul.

Whether you are a seasoned practitioner or a curious newcomer, this program promises an evening filled with spiritual bliss and inner harmony. We look forward to sharing this wonderful journey of devotion with you!

long_description:
Welcome!!

Meditation + Tea is a monthly gathering, for women of color to meditate and converse about cultivating more joy in our lives over a cup of delicious herbal tea.

This relaxed and informal gathering begins with a guided meditation designed to relieve stress, build community, and create space to unwind the narratives that block the flow of joy.
We will deepen the connection between mind, body, and heart through meditation, followed by conversation about living with meaningful joy over a cup of delicious herbal tea. (Our blends are cultivated and created by Ursula and Stephanie and shared for your enjoyment)

Our June gathering will be an evening of soulful movement meditation designed to help you reconnect with your body, breath, and inner rhythm.

Guided by a curated playlist featuring artists like Mariah the Scientist, Leon Thomas, Brent Faiyaz, Jazmine Sullivan, India Arie, Jill Scott, and other soulful R&B artists, we’ll move through an evening of slow flow, emotional presence, reflection, and release.

No dance experience is needed. This is not about performance or choreography, but about listening inward, moving intuitively, and allowing the body to guide the experience. We’ll close the evening with tea and reflective connection in community.

Come as you are. Move as you need. Leave feeling more rooted, softened, and alive.

$5 fee can be submitted via CashApp @ $meditationtea to secure your spot.

Space is limited.

long_description:
Hey Poetry Lovers!

This group is on a roll. Here’s the gist:

We meet at the **Capital One Café in Chinatown** from **12pm - 2pm** every other week.

For enrichment, we start by reading and reflecting on a **“published poem”**, suggested by someone in the group. No advance preparation is necessary. But feel free to check out some of the poems we’ve read [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSyE_wCLQCPHRrKmN5F9tOIeeRQUZESxjRXGVBoCF2uU8Gm0_d0uECiCBCQXEy6ksxfsBOhtRIOpW3T/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true&widget=true&headers=false%22%3E%3C/iframe%3E). Or submit suggestions for future meetings [here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSexGc2Z2Kp6bZW0D3_hfJ7NUUkfNHf7TXX-43FglCeBd9EF2Q/viewform?usp=send_form).

Next, we **share our work and offer feedback**. Depending on attendance, everyone gets \~10 minutes to use as they like. (No need to share, though; you’re welcome to come even if you prefer just to listen.)

We maintain a **Discord server** to help share our work and communicate outside our bi-weekly meet-ups. If you haven’t used Discord before, take a moment to download it and create an account before arriving. When we meet you on Saturday, we will add you to our server, the “DC Poetry Workshop”, and can help you navigate the app if you have questions.

Finally, if you plan on sharing a poem, consider how you will do so. Some options include:

* Print 5-10 copies to distribute in person
* Take and share screenshots in the Discord chat.
* Copy the poem into a google doc, change sharing settings to “anyone with link”, and copy the google doc link into the Discord chat.

Most importantly, we’re excited to meet you!

Catch you on Saturday,

Diego / Ian / Cayden / Nate / Otasha / Lia / An

long_description:
Socrates Café meets twice a month. Though this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, morality, and the first principles of things.

Prior to each meeting we vote online for the questions we will discuss. That way, we will have enough time to ruminate on them and have more in-depth conversations. If you RSVP to a meeting, you may post your question in the event comments section below. I'll send out a survey for voting a few days prior to the meetup. We discuss two questions each night. So you will get to cast two votes in the survey.

When we meet, we break into smaller groups of five to seven to discuss the top two vote-getters. Each group discusses one question for around 45-50 minutes, and we then take a short break. After reconvening, each group moves on to its second question.

Hope to see you there!

-Brian

long_description:
Hello friends! We're excited to host this summer outdoors, fingers crossed for a good, not-smokey day. We love this South Asian cookbook for its emphasis on local, family-run, sustainable agriculture and homey recipes from the same families.

**Official cookbook blurb:**
From Diaspora Co., the progressive spice company rooted in flavor and equity, comes a cookbook celebrating beautiful, simple, and seasonal cooking with 85 recipes adapted from India and Sri Lanka’s best family spice farms.
Diaspora Co. sources the most flavorful, fresh spices in the world from 150 regenerative farms across South Asia—from elders, indigenous communities, young changemakers, and brilliant multi-generational farming families across India and Sri Lanka who are leading the way in sustainable and climate change–resistant agriculture. Filled with culinary storytelling, *The Diaspora Co. Cookbook* highlights these farmers and their spices with profiles and evocative photography, plus 85 recipes for simple, seasonal, and powerfully delicious meals.

CEO and founder Sana Javeri Kadri and recipe writer Asha Loupy realized that eating with the people who grow our spices unveiled a whole new dimension in our cooking. For instance, the Mir family, who works all year to grow and harvest their saffron, shared not only their technique for blooming the vibrant spice and how to make sure every thread is fully utilized, but their unforgettably delicious dishes. Adapted for a global pantry, these recipes share the warmth of true South Asian home cooking at its truest and tastiest, starting with chutneys & pickles, snacks, and veggies, traveling through to mains from the sea and from the land, rice and breads, and ending with drinks and desserts.

long_description:
*Shambhala Boston's LGBTQ+ meditation group provides a welcoming environment for individuals of diverse sexual orientation and gender identity who are interested in exploring the teachings and principles of meditation and Buddhism.*

We provide an open space for genuine exploration of how these teachings can be incorporated into everyday life. Mixing our sense of self with the dharma can provide a powerful path toward the development of maitri, or friendliness, towards one’s self and others; it allows the opportunity to touch into who we are, open and share our hearts, and learn from each other.

The evening begins with a period of meditation practice, followed by group discussion on a suggested topic. Individuals of all spiritual-contemplative backgrounds are welcome, as well as those interested in learning more about meditation practice. The LGBTQ+ meditation group offers both a gateway for newcomers and a dynamic program for established practitioners. When we practice together, not only do we gain support in the process of self-discovery, but we can also deepen our understanding of how we are all interconnected.

Donations to the Center are welcome but not required. Please note that our building is not currently wheelchair accessible.

Registration is not required. For more information, click here: https://boston.shambhala.org/lgbtq/

long_description:
This event will be online on [YouTube](https://youtu.be/0KA1MIUltLo) and in-person (New York City). **The speaker and live stream starts at 7:30 pm ET**. In-person attendees may arrive as early as 7 pm ET. If arriving late, please leave a comment on this page and someone will come down ASAP.

**Description**
Every product we ship carries a worldview. "Efficiency is paramount." "Scale is the goal." "User engagement is the gateway.” Most of us don’t pause to reflect on what foundations we're building within ourselves. Stuff that feels too nebulous and exists out there, instead of in us, in here.

This isn't a talk about "bad actors." It's about the rest of us. The well-intentioned designers, PMs, and engineers whose unexamined defaults quietly shape what gets built, who it serves, and who it harms.

Drawing on indigenous learnings from Aotearoa New Zealand, and examples from accessibility and AI design, we'll explore what happens when we treat worldview work as foundational rather than optional.

Elina Ashimbayeva is determined to find hope amid humanity's existential crisis! Join Elina! This session will focus on examples and allow people to interact with each other to reflect on our individual and team practices and worldviews.
Because you can't change a practice without first changing the soil it grows in.

Attendees will leave with ...

* A clearer view of the worldviews running underneath your own work
* Language to name them with your team
* Examples of how different worldviews produce radically different products - especially in AI and accessibility
* A small set of tools and prompts for doing worldview work as part of practice, not separate from it.

**Presenter bio**
[Elina Ashimbayeva](https://www.linkedin.com/in/elina-ashimbayeva/) is a product manager, community builder, and facilitator with over a decade of work across healthcare, education, and social impact. Originally from Kazakhstan and Aotearoa New Zealand, she is now based in New York. Elina has led

***Transmutation*** **is the energetic and psycho-spiritual process of changing the nature, frequency, or purpose of an energy form within the body-mind system. Rather than suppress or release energy, the practitioner recycles and refines it, often channeling it to higher centers (chakras, glands, or awareness fields)**

Just over 20 years ago I received my Kundalini Yoga Teachers Training certification after a very challenging year. Prior to entering Teachers Training I had never actually taken a Yoga class but somehow I thought it was a good idea to go head first into what is arguably the most challenging style of Yoga. The reason Kundalini Yoga is in my opinion the most challenging style has little to do with the Asanas, or postures, taught but more to do with the incredible concentration required to properly engage a Kundalini Yoga meditation. The concentration one cultivates while practicing KY is the key to much of the extraordinary benefit one receives from a long term practice of this style...

Most of us go about our day without realizing what is happening energetically and by the end of the day we can feel rather drained. This draining of energy of course is partially due to how we expend energy throughout the day but also due to how we loose our center as the day wears on, assuming we actually know how to center ourselves in the first place. When we do a Kundalini Yoga Meditation there are many areas we place our focus. We might have our eyes on the tip of the nose, with our hands in a mudra, while chanting a precise mantra and of course all the while needing to maintain an erect spine. What all theses various point of focus does is to shunt our vital life force back into the body's central channel which will then create a powerful internal spiritual/energetic pressure which can activate the higher energy centers granting us access to our innate sensitivity, extra sensory perceptions, and deep inner peace.

organizer: Houston Inner Loop Classic Book Club
long_description:
Join us for a deep-dive discussion of Middlemarch by George Eliot — widely considered one of the greatest novels ever written.
Set in a provincial English town during the 1830s, Middlemarch explores love, idealism, money, politics, status, ambition, self-delusion, and the quiet compromises that shape a life. The novel follows multiple intertwined characters, especially Dorothea Brooke and Dr. Lydgate, as they struggle between who they hoped to become and the realities of society and human nature.
This is a rich, rewarding novel that becomes more powerful the more life experience you bring to it. Expect sharp psychological insight, memorable characters, social commentary, and surprisingly modern observations about relationships and personal growth.
Length:
• Approximately 850–900 pages depending on edition
• Estimated reading time: 28–40 hours
• Recommended pace: 60–80 pages per week over 2–3 months
Perfect for readers interested in:
• Classic literature
• Human psychology
• Philosophy & ethics
• Relationships & marriage
• Social ambition & status
• Deep character studies
Bring your thoughts, favorite passages, questions, and disagreements. Even if you don’t finish the entire book, come anyway — the discussion itself will be worthwhile.

**Outdoor Kirtan @ Gasworks Park!**
Join us against a beautiful backdrop of the Seattle skyline as we take a journey into sacred sound meditation and mantra.

**What is Kirtan?**
Kirtan is a form of musical meditation rooted in call-and-response singing. It involves repeating simple mantras or phrases set to music, often accompanied by instruments like the harmonium, drums, and cymbals. Open to all backgrounds, kirtan offers a space for collective expression, connection, and relaxation through sound and rhythm. You don’t need to be a singer—just come with an open heart and join in at your own comfort level.

**We will meet at Bhakti Studio across the street and walk to the park together!**

**WHAT TO EXPECT**
Kirtan Soulfest is simply a transcendental party guaranteed to uplift you mentally, physically, and emotionally. The sacred mantras chanted in a call-and-response manner is the prescribed method given in the Vedas to link the inner divinity within all of us. This link connects us to the real happiness, peace and love we are all searching for.
Come with an open heart, dance and leave with an overflow of LOVE!

**WHAT IS MANTRA MEDITATION?**
Mantra Meditation is a type of Sound Bath and Yoga which is an immersive experience combining powerful soundwaves and group singing/chanting to help individuals better connect with their inner selves. Yoga means to unite, Mantra Meditation will help unite your mind to your body and soul.
The sounds and singing during a Mantra Meditation session are an invitation to journey into a deeper state of consciousness as an opportunity to gain perspective on what's going on within you. The goal of the experience is to invite deep relaxation, restoration and explore self-inquiry and self-discovery.

Join us for brunch with a Latin twist at all-day Rosa's Diner!

**From Eater DC**

After going dark for two years, a tony corner of downtown D.C. makes a comeback today, Friday, May 22, as Rosa's Diner, an all-day ode to Americana classics with Latin twists.

The glamorous Victorian row house attached to the Moxy hotel was restored to its original glory back in 2023 to welcome Atlas Restaurant Group's polished oyster bar Parlor Victoria, which didn’t last long.

The brick-framed building’s latest culinary chapter falls under the watch of executive chef Francisco Pomalaza, who’s cooked in New York, Chicago, and his hometown of Miami – but never before in D.C. His newest post in a 9-to-5 corridor is a big departure from his recent beachside gig at Florida’s Havana Beach Bar & Grill at the Pearl Hotel.

“I felt that this was more freedom for creativity. There are so many countries to touch on,” says Pomalaza, who’s Peruvian. “It’s still an American theme, but influenced by Latin flavors.”

See: his eggs “Benedict” – which is actually a pupusa topped with beef birria and aji amarillo hollandaise.

Unlike its short-lived predecessor, which served seafood towers and steaks in an opulent setting, Rosa’s Diner dresses things down a bit with retro bar stools, slick green booths, and a walk-up counter with a full coffee program and a case stocked with its house-made pastries. A full bar spotlights spirits like a Latin gin made from Malbec grapes.

The Moon in July is often referred to as the Buck Moon, a powerful symbol of natural cycles, renewal, and growth. Just as the buck sheds its antlers to make space for what is next, this lunar energy invites us to gently release emotional weight, outdated patterns, and anything we are no longer meant to carry.

· Ceremonial cacao to gently open the heart, lovingly prepared by Jason

· Conscious breathwork to support emotional release and nervous system balance
· Guided meditation to deepen inner awareness and intuition
· Immersive 432 Hz crystal bowl sound bath
· Grounding chimes, gongs, and sacred sound instruments

long_description:
**Join us in a discussion about the book** **"Man's Search for Meaning" by Viktor Frankl!**

The book club also now has a Discord server! Feel free to join to keep up the discussion between meetups! [l](https://discord.gg/EnrvhBMZ)
https://discord.gg/M2NZq2Xvce

You don't have to buy anything, but the venue has light pub fare, ice cream, and a great selection of both alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. They also allow outside restaurant food, so bring something to eat if you need sustenance!

**Book Description:**

This seminal book, which has been called “one of the outstanding contributions to psychological thought” by Carl Rogers and “one of the great books of our time” by Harold Kushner, has been translated into more than fifty languages and sold over sixteen million copies. “An enduring work of survival literature,” according to the New York Times, Viktor Frankl’s riveting account of his time in the Nazi concentration camps, and his insightful exploration of the human will to find meaning in spite of the worst adversity, has offered solace and guidance to generations of readers since it was first published in 1946. At the heart of Frankl’s theory of logotherapy (from the Greek word for “meaning”) is a conviction that the primary human drive is not pleasure, as Freud maintained, but rather the discovery and pursuit of what the individual finds meaningful. Today, as new generations face new challenges and an ever more complex and uncertain world, Frankl’s classic work continues to inspire us all to find significance in the very act of living, in spite of all obstacles.

## **Urban Reset La Dera Park: Walking Meditation & Movement**

**Hosted by Monique Marie \| The Free Spirit Yogi**

### **From "Doing" into "Being"**

In the heart of the city lies a pocket of peace. Join us at **Ladera Park** for an intimate, guided journey designed to help you shed the noise of the week and return to your center. This isn't just a yoga class; it’s a curated experience of stillness, nature, and community.

### **The Experience**

Our reset is divided into four intentional phases:

* **The Silent Walk (40 Minutes):** We begin at our meeting spot with a single chime of the singing bowl. You will receive a **Mindful Focus Card**—a tactile, hand-held guide to anchor your thoughts as you wander toward the oaks. Every few minutes, the chime will ring again, calling you to take one deep, conscious breath, notice exactly where you are, and continue your journey in silence.
* **The Movement (35 Minutes):** Once we reach the dappled shade of the oak grove, we transition from the internal journey to the physical. We will move through a grounding yoga flow designed to integrate the peace of your walk into your body.
* **The Integration (5 Minutes):** We conclude our journey by bringing the stillness of the park into the center of our being. As we settle into our final resting pose, the "doing" is officially done. This is your time to absorb the frequency of the trees, the rhythm of your breath, and the shift in your energy.
* The play. Lets challenge our balance by trying arm balances, inversions and new asanas to deepen our practice.
* The departure. One final collective breath to share gratitude.

### **What’s Provided**

To ensure you can remain fully "hands-free" and present, we provide:

* **Yoga Mat Backpacks:** To ensure you can fully immerse yourself in the walking meditation, we provide complimentary use of our Yoga Mat Backpacks for the duration of the experience.
* **Mindful Focus Cards:** Yours to use during the event.

long_description:
Within each of us lies a dream that carries us toward Africa. Whether it began in childhood or later in life, the image of the savanna, snow-capped mountains, and untamed wildlife stirs curiosity, emotion, and the desire for adventure. Kilimanjaro, the rooftop of the African continent, is the symbol of that call — a legendary mountain, a natural wonder that seems lifted from an African fairytale. With its imposing silhouette surrounded by tropical forests and arid savannas, Kilimanjaro offers a one-of-a-kind experience — a journey from equatorial jungle to a landscape resembling the polar tundra.

It's an ascent that leaves a mark not only physically but emotionally. As you climb, you don't just reach a summit — you rediscover a part of yourself. The peak offers a new horizon: clearer, broader, and more confident.

From a technical standpoint, Kilimanjaro is the most accessible peak of the famous Seven Summits and Seven Volcanoes. It doesn't require mountaineering skills and is successfully climbed each year by people of all ages — from 6 to 83 years old. The trails are well-maintained, logistics are excellent, and porters carry most of the gear, making the experience both comfortable and achievable.

For those who want to extend their African journey, the expedition can be followed by a spectacular safari in Tarangire and Ngorongoro — the land of great migrations, lions, and elephants, an unmatched natural spectacle.

This is more than just a vacation — it's a journey that leaves a deep mark on your soul and gently changes the way you see the world.

Highlights:
• Uhuru Peak (5,895m) – Roof of Africa
• Journey from tropical rainforest to arctic-alpine zone
• Machame Route – one of the most scenic paths
• Sunrise summit attempt under a star-filled sky
• Certificate of achievement upon completion
• Optional: Safari extension in Tarangire and Ngorongoro Crater

long_description:
Join us on July 25 at Sarva in Back Bay as we discuss *The Loneliness of Sonia & Sunny* by Kiran Desai.

Nearly twenty years after winning the Booker Prize for *The Inheritance of Loss*, Kiran Desai returns with an ambitious novel that spans continents, generations, and cultures. At its heart is the story of Sonia and Sunny, two young Indians whose lives intersect between India and the United States as they search for love, purpose, and a sense of belonging in an increasingly globalized world. What begins as a chance encounter unfolds into a sweeping exploration of family, identity, migration, class, and the ties that connect us across time and distance.
Desai's novel is both an intimate love story and an expansive family saga, filled with vivid characters, sharp observations, and reflections on what it means to build a life between cultures. Through Sonia and Sunny's journeys, the novel examines loneliness not simply as isolation, but as a universal human experience shaped by history, family expectations, and the search for connection.

As always, our discussion will be relaxed, welcoming, and accompanied by excellent food. Whether you read every page, are still making your way through this doorstopper of a novel, or are simply curious about contemporary South Asian literature, we'd love to have you join us.
📖 Book: *The Loneliness of Sonia & Sunny* by Kiran Desai
📍 Location: Sarva, Back Bay
📅 Date: July 25
Come for the fiction, stay for the food and conversation.

**BAPS Detroit Mandir 22nd Patotsav (Anniversary)**

Celebrate the 22nd anniversary of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in the Detroit area, beautifully coinciding with India's Independence Day.

This grand celebration will feature:

- **2:00 PM** – Vedic Mahapuja (sacred fire ceremony)
- **2:00 – 5:00 PM** – Annakut Darshan (offering of hundreds of food items to the deities)
- **4:00 PM** – Patotsav Sabha (cultural assembly with addresses by visiting swamis)

The Patotsav marks the sacred anniversary of the mandir's murti pratishtha (consecration of the deities) and is one of the most auspicious events of the year.

**Details:**
- Date: Saturday, August 15, 2026
- Location: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Canton, MI
- Admission: Free and open to all

Special prasad and celebrations throughout the day. All families welcome.

title: Diwali Celebrations — BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir Atlanta
description: Grand Diwali celebration at BAPS Atlanta with traditional lighting, cultural performances, and community feast.

The festival brings together Atlanta's large Indian diaspora for the cherished Festival of Lights tradition. Youth and adult cultural programs, fireworks, and festive sweets make it a complete Diwali experience.

title: Diwali Festival — Shiva Vishnu Temple Livermore

A must-attend for Bay Area families.
venue_info: 1232 Arrowhead Ave, Livermore. All-day event. Expect very large crowds — shuttle service often provided from overflow parking. Prasadam and festival food available.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Sri Venkateswara Temple, Pittsburgh
description: Diwali at America's oldest traditional Hindu temple with Lakshmi Puja and grand celebrations.
long_description: Celebrate Diwali at the historic Sri Venkateswara Temple in Penn Hills — the first traditional Hindu temple in America. Special Lakshmi Puja, Sahasranama archana, cultural performances, and fireworks make this one of Pittsburgh's most significant Hindu celebrations.

venue_info: 3818 212th St SE, Bothell, WA 98021. Free parking. All-day event. Prasadam served.

title: Diwali Celebrations — BAPS Mandir, Los Angeles

long_description: Celebrate Diwali at the stunning BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Chino Hills. The temple's pink sandstone and white marble architecture shines brilliantly when illuminated for Diwali. Programs include Lakshmi Puja, Chopda Puja for business owners, cultural shows, and spectacular fireworks. One of LA's most attended Hindu celebrations.

venue_info: 117 Waverly St, Ashland, MA 01721. All-day event. Ample parking. Prasadam and festival food.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Sri Meenakshi Temple, Houston

The grand evening features elaborate Lakshmi Puja, thousands of diyas, cultural programs, a fireworks display, and community dinner. The temple's impressive Dravidian architecture provides a stunning backdrop for the Festival of Lights.
venue_info: 17130 McLean Rd, Pearland, TX. Free parking. Large grounds accommodate thousands of visitors.

title: Diwali Festival — DFW Hindu Temple, Irving

long_description: Celebrate Diwali at one of Southern California's most scenic temples. A unique and unforgettable Diwali experience in the LA area.
venue_info: 1600 Las Virgenes Canyon Rd, Calabasas. All-day event. Parking fills up fast — arrive early. Prasadam available.

title: Diwali Celebrations — BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Milpitas
description: Grand Diwali celebration at the BAPS Mandir with lighting ceremony, cultural program, and community feast.
long_description: BAPS Milpitas hosts its spectacular Diwali celebration, the Festival of Lights. The evening features thousands of diyas illuminating the mandir, a cultural program with devotional performances, fireworks, and a community dinner. One of the most visually stunning Diwali celebrations in the Bay Area.
venue_info: BAPS Mandir, Milpitas. Large parking facility. Expect heavy crowds — arrive early. Modest dress code required inside the mandir.

title: Diwali Mela — BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir Houston

venue_info: BAPS Mandir, Houston. Large parking lot. Family-friendly. Modest dress code inside the mandir.

Festive food stalls offer traditional sweets and savories. One of the Bay Area's most well-attended Diwali celebrations.
venue_info: 450 Persian Drive, Sunnyvale. Free parking. Expect heavy crowds — arrive early for best parking. Dress in festive attire.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Bharatiya Temple, Troy MI
